note: Tier 1, from a position. The pay question with a payment (118.12, 118.12a): A casts Grizzly Bears, B answers with Dazzling Denial ("Counter target spell unless its controller pays {2}. If you control a Bird, counter that spell unless its controller pays {4} instead."); B controls no Bird, so as Denial resolves A is asked whether to pay {2}, pays it with two Forests (608.2g), and the Bears is not countered and resolves. Tapped status and the mana pool are tier-2 facts and are not stated. The position is stipulated (spec 2.4), not reached by ordinary play.

transitions.note: A creature spell may be cast in A's main phase with priority and an empty stack (302.1, 117.1a). 601.2a: the Bears moves from A's hand to the top of the stack; it has no targets (601.2c). 601.2g, 601.2h: A taps two Forests for {G} each (305.6, 106.4) and pays {1}{G}. 601.2i, 117.3c: A, who had priority, receives priority again; A passes (implied, 117.3d) and B, next in turn order, receives priority. One pass resolves nothing (117.4).

Dazzling Denial is an instant, so B may cast it with priority while the Bears is on the stack (117.1a). 601.2a, 601.2c: it goes on top of the stack (405.2) targeting the Bears spell. 601.2g, 601.2h: B taps two Islands for {U} each (305.6) and pays {1}{U}. 117.3c: B receives priority and passes (implied); A passes (implied); B's casting was an action between the earlier pass and these, so these two passes are the succession of 117.4 and Denial, the top object, resolves (608.1). 608.2b: its target is still on the stack and legal. B controls no Bird, so the instruction is "counter target spell unless its controller pays {2}"; 118.12a reads that as "its controller may pay {2}; if they don't, counter it", and the payment is a cost paid while Denial resolves (118.12). The Bears' controller, A, is asked; spec 4.2: Denial is still on the stack (above the Bears) at this boundary.

608.2g: offered the option to pay mana, A activates the mana abilities of the two remaining Forests (605.3a, 305.6) and pays {2} (118.12). Since A paid, the counter instruction does not happen (118.12a); the Bears stays on the stack. 608.2n: as the final part of its resolution the instant Dazzling Denial goes to its owner's graveyard. 117.3b: the active player, A, receives priority after a resolution (not B, Denial's controller). A passes and B passes (implied, 117.4) and the Bears resolves: it has no targets, so it becomes a permanent and enters the battlefield under the control of its controller A (608.3a), which is its owner, so no controller fact is written. 117.3b: A, the active player, receives priority again, in the precombat main phase with an empty stack. The mana pool emptied as each payment spent it (tier 2, not stated).
